results.question: What are the prerequisites for Deep Learning (TDIS22)?
results.expected_answer: 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Computer Science/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering, plus completed Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics for Intelligent Systems and Machine Learning (7.5 credits each) or equivalent; English proficiency.
results.answer: Passed at least 90 credits within the major subject Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or equivalent, or at least 150 credits from the Computer Science and Engineering programme. Also required: completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits), Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), and Machine Learning (7.5 credits) or equivalent, plus proof of English proficiency [1].

results.question: How is TARI29 graded?
results.expected_answer: 5, 4, 3 or U; final grade only after all assessments are completed.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits) is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. The final grade is based on a balanced set of assessments and is only issued after all assessments are satisfactorily completed [1].

results.question: What grading scale does the Communication and Artificial Intelligence course use?
results.expected_answer: A, B, C, D, E, FX or F; A to E are passing grades.
results.answer: The Communication and Artificial Intelligence (LAIK15) course is graded A, B, C, D, E, FX or F, where A to E are passing grades [1]. The registration table also lists the individual written exam and written assignment as graded A/B/C/D/E/FX/F, while the group presentation is graded U/G [3].

results.question: What do I need before taking Mathematical Statistics?
results.expected_answer: General entry requirements and completed Single Variable Calculus, 7.5 credits, or equivalent.
results.answer: You need the general entry requirements and a completed Single Variable Calculus course worth 7.5 credits, or an equivalent course [1].

results.question: How is the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence course examined?
results.expected_answer: Active participation in seminars and group discussions, and three assignments; graded 5, 4, 3 or U.
results.answer: The course is graded 5, 4, 3 or U. Examination consists of active participation in seminars and group discussions, plus three assignments: an investigation of a fairness-related ethical challenge in a practical case, a group presentation debating an ethical topic, and a written debate assignment. The final grade requires satisfactory completion of all assessments.

results.question: How is the final project in computer science examined?
results.expected_answer: Written report, oral presentation, opposition on another group's work, and mandatory elements; graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail.
results.answer: The final project in computer science (TEXV23) is graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail, and is examined through a written report, an oral presentation of the report, a review and discussion of another group's work (opponering), and fulfilment of mandatory elements. The grade is set according to a special assessment template [2]. The written report is the most important part of the assessment, and the report is filed in DiVA [4].

results.question: Does the Deep Learning course include a project?
results.expected_answer: Yes: one project with tutoring and two project seminars (design and final presentation).
results.answer: Yes. The Deep Learning course includes one project, along with project tutoring and two project seminars [1]. The project is worth 5.5 credits and is graded 5/4/3/U [4].

results.question: Which language is the Artificial Intelligence course TARI29 taught in?
results.expected_answer: English.
results.answer: The Artificial Intelligence course (TARI29) is taught in English [1].

results.question: What topics does TARI29 cover?
results.expected_answer: Traditional AI and search, reasoning under uncertainty, evolutionary optimization, intelligent agents, game theory and minimax, Markov decision processes.
results.answer: TARI29 (Artificial Intelligence) covers traditional AI (GOFAI) topics such as problem representation, production systems, search, planning, expert systems, automated reasoning, propositional and predicate logic, and resolution [1]. It also covers reasoning under uncertainty (Bayesian inferencing), evolutionary optimization programming, intelligent agents, basic game theory with minimax, and agents for Markov decision processes [1].

results.question: What are the entry requirements for Mathematics for Intelligent Systems?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, IT or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent, including at least 15 credits of mathematics.
results.answer: Applicants need a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS credits) from an accredited university, with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Informatics, Information Systems, Information Technology, or Electrical Engineering (with relevant computer engineering courses), or equivalent. The degree must include at least 15 credits in mathematics. Proof of English proficiency is also required [1].

results.question: Can the credit requirements for the final project work be waived?
results.expected_answer: The programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements, but not from the required Bachelor degree.
results.answer: Yes, partly. The programme manager can grant an exemption from the points requirements under the Prerequisites, but no exemption will be made to the required Bachelor degree [1].

results.question: When can I start my final project work?
results.expected_answer: After the examiner's approval.
results.answer: You can start your final project work only after you meet the prerequisites in the course syllabus and submit the registration form to the course coordinator [1]. The examiner must approve the registration and project description before you can initiate the project [1][2]. For Computer Science (TEXV23), the project may begin after the examiner's approval [3].

results.question: Which courses must I have taken before Intelligent Optimization and Problem Solving?
results.expected_answer: Artificial Intelligence, 7.5 credits, among the listed courses, plus 90 credits in Computer Engineering/Electrical Engineering or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: You need to have passed at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering or Electrical Engineering (with relevant Computer Engineering courses), or at least 150 credits in Computer Science and Engineering. You also need to have taken Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Knowledge Representation and the Semantic Web (7.5 credits), or equivalent courses. Proof of English proficiency is required [1].

results.question: How is the final grade decided in Deep Learning?
results.expected_answer: Graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail; project credits come from the report, two presentations and active participation in two seminars.
results.answer: In Deep Learning (TDIS22), the course is graded 5, 4, 3 or Fail [1]. The final grade is determined by the presentations and the project report [1]. The project report grade is based on both its collaborative part and the individual part [1]. The final grade is issued only when all course units have been passed [2].

results.question: What kind of teaching does Data Science Programming have?
results.expected_answer: Lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, in English.
results.answer: Data Science Programming is taught through lectures, quizzes, assignments, workshops and tutoring, and the teaching is conducted in English [1].

results.question: What happens if I am late to my exam?
results.expected_answer: Doors are closed and locked 10 minutes before the exam starts; be on site no later than 10 minutes before.
results.answer: If you arrive after the doors close 10 minutes before the exam, you will not be admitted until the second admission, 30 minutes into the exam. An invigilator will check your ID and give brief instructions before you are seated. If you arrive more than 30 minutes late, you will not be allowed to take the exam, and no excuses are accepted.

results.question: How many days before an exam must I register?
results.expected_answer: No later than 10 days before; unregistered students cannot take the exam.
results.answer: You must register no later than 10 days before the examination date. [1][2] Targeted educational support must also be registered no later than 10 days in advance. [3]

results.question: Which IDs are accepted at exams?
results.expected_answer: Valid Swedish driver's license, Swedish passport, Swedish national ID card, or JU card marked Identity Card; valid foreign passports under conditions.
results.answer: Accepted IDs for exams are a valid Swedish driver's license, a valid Swedish passport, a valid Swedish national ID card, or a valid JU card marked with "Identity Card". Foreign passports must be valid, plastic wrapped, and in English, French, or Spanish. BankID and Freja eID+ are not accepted.

results.question: Can I identify myself with BankID at an exam?
results.expected_answer: No. BankID and Freja eID+ are not physical identification.
results.answer: No. BankID does not count as physical identification and is not accepted as a valid ID during exams. Only approved physical IDs, such as a valid Swedish driver's license, passport, national ID card, or a JU card marked "Identity Card", are accepted [1].

results.question: Can I bring snacks into the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Food and drinks are allowed, but no nuts, smelly or smudging food, and no fragrances.
results.answer: Yes, you can bring food and drinks to the exam hall, but not nuts or foods containing nuts, and not food that smells or smudges [1]. Only food and drinks may be on the desk along with permitted aids and your ID [2].

results.question: When am I allowed to leave the exam hall?
results.expected_answer: Not during the first 30 minutes.
results.answer: You may not leave the exam hall during the first 30 minutes [1]. After that, you may leave only with an invigilator's permission or for a restroom visit, following the hall's restroom rules; leaving for any other reason, or without permission, counts as cancelling your exam [1][2]. When the invigilators announce that time is up, you must stop writing immediately [4].

results.question: How long does it take to get my exam results?
results.expected_answer: Results are reported via Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam, except for special reasons.
results.answer: Exam results are normally notified to students through Ladok no later than 20 working days after the examination occasion. If special reasons exist, they may be notified later, but no later than 14 days before the next examination occasion, and students must be told in writing about the delay.

results.question: Can I keep my student accommodation during a study break?
results.expected_answer: No.
results.answer: No. If you are granted a study break, you are not allowed to keep your student accommodation [1].

results.question: What does a study break mean for my residence permit?
results.expected_answer: JU informs the Migration Agency, which revokes the residence permit, so the student must leave Sweden.
results.answer: If you are granted a study break (approved leave from studies), Jönköping University informs the Swedish Migration Agency, which will revoke your residence permit, and you must then leave Sweden. It is recommended that you speak with your programme's study counsellor before applying [1].

results.question: What disciplinary measures can be taken against a student?
results.expected_answer: Warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension; expulsion is also possible.
results.answer: The disciplinary measures that can be taken against a student are a warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension [4]. A student may also be expelled from studies on specific grounds, such as mental disturbance, alcohol or drug abuse, or being found guilty of a serious crime [5]. Decisions to issue a warning or suspension, or to expel a student, can be appealed to the Board of Appeals [1].

results.question: Which decisions can I appeal to the Board of Appeals?
results.expected_answer: Disciplinary Committee decisions (warning, suspension, expulsion) and listed faculty/school decisions.
results.answer: You can appeal Disciplinary Committee decisions to give a warning or suspension, or to expel you [1]. You can also appeal faculty decisions, made through Study Administration, to reject an applicant for not meeting entry requirements, to refuse an exception or deferred enrolment, to transfer credits, to refuse a degree or course certificate (except where the student is suspended indefinitely for unpaid tuition fees), or to withdraw admission due to incorrect information provided by the applicant [1]. Faculties' refusals of exemption from a compulsory element, leave from studies, or doctoral supervision rights, decisions under the Discrimination Act, and refusals of tuition fee refunds based on special circumstances are also appealable [1][2]. However, the Disciplinary Committee instructions state that its expulsion decisions may not be appealed, which conflicts with [1], so check the current rules for expulsion cases [4].

results.question: How do I pay the application fee for a local admission?
results.expected_answer: To JU, by approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) via the web payment system.
results.answer: For local admissions, pay the application fee to JU. You can use an approved bank card (VISA/MasterCard) through the web-based payment solution in the online application form, or use another method agreed with JU [1]. The fee must be paid no later than the deadline for supplementary information, or the application will only be considered if time permits [1].

results.question: What does § 5 of the disciplinary committee instructions say?
results.expected_answer: The disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations and suspension.
results.answer: Section 5 says the disciplinary measures are warning, exclusion from examinations, and suspension [1]. A warning is given in writing, and exclusion from examinations bars the student from University examinations for a continuous period of up to six months [1]. Suspension bars the student from classes, examinations, and other education activities for up to six months in total, and may apply to access to certain facilities [1]. Any decision must state its grounds [1].

results.question: What does section 2.15 of the education regulations say about grades?
results.expected_answer: Results are notified via Ladok within 20 working days of the examination.
results.answer: Section 2.15 says exam results must be notified to students through Ladok no later than 20 working days after the exam. For special reasons, notification may be later but no later than 14 days before the next exam occasion, and students must be told in writing. The examiner is responsible for reporting results to Ladok, and feedback must be offered at least 14 days before the next ordinary exam. Test answers and grade notifications must protect students' legal rights and integrity, and equal treatment should be considered when designing examinations.

results.question: What are the TARI29 entry requirements?
results.expected_answer: Bachelor's degree (180 credits) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering, or 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering.
results.answer: Applicants need at least a bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) with at least 90 credits in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or Electrical Engineering (or equivalent), or at least 150 credits from Computer Science and Engineering. The degree must include a minimum of 15 credits in mathematics, and proof of English proficiency is required [1].

results.question: What is LAIK15 about?
results.expected_answer: Media and communication and artificial intelligence, including representations of AI and generative AI in media.
results.answer: LAIK15, Communication and Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits, first-cycle, valid from spring 2025), covers research perspectives on AI, media and cultural industries, generative AI as a tool for producing texts, representations of AI, and its impact in different contexts [3][4]. Students learn to describe AI representations in public and popular spheres and to critically reflect on AI's opportunities and limitations in media and communication [5][1]. It is taught within Media and Communication Science [3].

results.question: Is TDPS22 taught in English?
results.expected_answer: Yes.
results.answer: Yes, the Data Science Programming (TDPS22) course is taught in English, according to the current version valid from 2025-01-01. [1]

results.question: What does § 28 of the disciplinary committee instructions allow?
results.expected_answer: A decision may always be appealed to the Board of Appeals if it contravenes the Discrimination Act.
results.answer: Section 28 allows a decision to be appealed to the Board of Appeals at any time, on the grounds that the decision contravenes specified sections of the Discrimination Act (2008:567). The same passage states that a Committee decision on expulsion may not be appealed.

results.question: Can I take Machine Learning (TMLS22) if my major is Computer Science?
results.expected_answer: Yes: the current (2025) syllabus includes Computer Science among the accepted majors; the 2024 version did not.
results.answer: Possibly. You need at least 90 credits within your major subject, Computer Science (or an equivalent), and completed Artificial Intelligence (7.5 credits) and Mathematics for Intelligent Systems (7.5 credits), or equivalent courses. You also need proof of English proficiency [2]. The course is taught in English [5].

results.question: How is Ethics of AI examined this year?
